This is also almost exactly the form the refusing reviewer named as defensible ('grounded, well-formed, content-bearing output that is simply wrong'). 'Anyway' carries the argumentative weight — it means 'notwithstanding those three properties' — and that contrast is precisely what the decomposition measures: the channel is defined by the three properties and still carries 87% of the loss. q2_is_the_carried_measurement_correctly_.baselines_reproduce_too: zs content-bearing 1,238 documents, tp 32 / fp 1,319 / fn 2,765; fs 1,130 documents, tp 110 / fp 1,135 / fn 2,636. q2_is_the_carried_measurement_correctly_.is_the_2003_of_2515_figure_stated_with_i: YES. The ledger limitation says: '2,003 of 2,515 error-bearing documents show both fp and fn, consistent with substitution, so mostly missing arguments is ruled out.' That is exactly what the number means and exactly as far as it reaches. A substitution produces one fp and one fn; a missing gold argument produces fn only; an extra argument produces fp only. 80% of error-bearing documents carry both, so a purely-missing-argument account is excluded — which is what is claimed, no more. It uses 'consistent with', which is one of the three phrasings the accepted plan's section 12.3 prescribes, and the same limitation immediately records that wrong-role, boundary and coreference errors share the identical signature and that section 12.1 has not been run. This is a correctly hedged carry, not a substitution claim in hedged clothing.
q2_is_the_carried_measurement_correctly_.is_the_over_generation_reading_sound: YES, and it is the sharper half. fp exceeds fn by 637 arguments, and 334 documents carry fp with no fn at all against 178 the other way. A pure in-role substitution keeps fp and fn equal; these are not equal. 'Systematic over-generation' is a fair description of a 637-argument excess over 2,515 error-bearing documents. The ledger states it as a measurement that 'points the other way' rather than as a new attribution, which is the correct register for a figure that has not been through section 12.1 either.

q8_are_the_section_11_and_12_disposition.verdict: The DECISIONS are the owner's and I do not re-litigate them. The REASONING is sound on every item except ONE, which is factually wrong. Required item R3.

the_factually_wrong_disposition.item: section 11.1, first row: 'mean vs maximum-frame document loss'
the_factually_wrong_disposition.claimed: **executed** — 'Done and reported. docs/plan3/certification-result.md records unweighted vs size-weighted group loss agreeing to within 0.0002-0.0011 on the certification split (amendment A2), which is the sensitivity this item asks for at the aggregation level that matters.'
the_factually_wrong_disposition.why_it_is_wrong: These are two different sensitivities on two different axes, and the one the plan asks for was not run. The accepted plan's section 4.1 defines the item precisely: 'If a source document contains multiple target frames, the primary group loss is the mean bounded frame loss declared in Plan 1. The strict sensitivity analysis uses MAXIMUM FRAME LOSS PER DOCUMENT.' That is mean-versus-max WITHIN a group, over the frames it contains. What A2 delivered — docs/plan3/certification-result.md line 182, 'Unweighted vs size-weighted group loss agree to within 0.0002-0.0011' — is how GROUP MEANS ARE COMBINED across groups into the population figure. Neither computation is a substitute for the other: A2 varies the weight on each group, the plan's item varies the statistic inside each group. Max-frame loss is a strictly larger quantity than mean-frame loss wherever a group holds more than one frame, and 3,152 documents across 1,396 groups means most groups hold more than one. The refusal record listed this item explicitly under 'NOT_moot_computable_now_at_zero_dollars_on_already_open_splits', naming it 'the section 4.1 strict sensitivity', and its own search for 'max_frame|maximum_frame' across evidence/, src/ and docs/ returned nothing. I repeated that search and confirm it still returns nothing.
the_factually_wrong_disposition.why_the_clause_at_the_end_gives_it_away: '...at the aggregation level that matters' concedes that a different aggregation level was measured. That is an argument for descoping the item, and it may well be a good one. It is not a basis for marking it **executed**. The defect O1 named was that mootness was ASSUMED rather than ruled; marking an unrun analysis 'executed' is the same substitution wearing a different label, and it is the only row in the document that does it.
the_factually_wrong_disposition.what_would_fix_it: See R3. Any of executed / descoped / moot is available to the owner on a correct ground; only 'executed' is unavailable, because it is not true.

dispositions_whose_reasoning_i_checked_a.11.1 exact vs normalized span matching —: Sound. Span matching is frozen by ADR 0006's extraction policy, and re-scoring the certified object after seeing the result is what section 8.5 forbids. Methodological ground, correctly given.
dispositions_whose_reasoning_i_checked_a.11.1 binary strict-failure certificate —: Sound in conclusion, slightly loose in reasoning. 'A certificate requires a feasible candidate; none exists' is stated as though feasibility under the primary loss settled feasibility under the strict loss, which does not follow in general. It does follow here, and by a wider margin: the strict-failure loss dominates the continuous loss pointwise, so a population whose continuous base risk is 0.607 (QA) cannot have a lower strict base risk, and the mean_loss_ceiling of 0.84 excludes it a fortiori. Right answer; the reason would be stronger stated that way. Not a required item.
dispositions_whose_reasoning_i_checked_a.11.1 completion-mean-NLL score — descope: Sound. The item is descriptive-only by its own terms, and the oracle risk-coverage curve already bounds what ANY threshold rule on ANY score could achieve at 2.0% acceptance, so a second score is measured against the same ceiling. Section 8.5's bar on an alternative score as a rescue is correctly cited.
dispositions_whose_reasoning_i_checked_a.11.1 accepted-output quality by distance: Sound. The unit is accepted outputs; selected_candidate is null and n_accepted is 0 for all three systems.
dispositions_whose_reasoning_i_checked_a.11.1 constrained decoding — moot, precon: Sound and checkable. The item is conditional on Plan 1 admitting constrained decoding as a structural-validity ablation; ADR 0002 descoped training ablations to a single seed. The condition never fired.
dispositions_whose_reasoning_i_checked_a.11.2 subgroup reporting — moot: Sound, and better than it had to be: it states what is NOT claimed — that subgroup analysis of LOSS across all predictions is possible and is being descoped rather than being impossible. That distinction is exactly what O1 asked for.
dispositions_whose_reasoning_i_checked_a.11.3 Spearman and AUROC/AUPRC — descoped: Sound as reasoning. The oracle risk-coverage curve bounds what any threshold rule could achieve, so a rank correlation is weaker evidence for the same conclusion, and adding a new statistic to an already-open split after the result is the post-hoc move ADR 0006's C4 guards against. Whether to run them anyway is the owner's call and I do not take it.
dispositions_whose_reasoning_i_checked_a.11.3 binned diagrams — descoped; selecti: Both sound. The selective-risk curves ARE risk-coverage-diagnostic and alpha-frontier, both committed with immutable artifacts that a prior reviewer regenerated byte-identically.
dispositions_whose_reasoning_i_checked_a.11.4 multiplicity — executed: Sound. H1/H2 are the only confirmatory comparisons and collapse to one finding; threshold adaptivity is inside SCoRC; alpha_frontier.json carries diagnostic_only and certifies_nothing; no subgroup claim exists to carry an uncorrected p-value.
dispositions_whose_reasoning_i_checked_a.12.1 — EXECUTE, not yet run: Sound, and the cost verification is real: all three prediction files and the RAMS archive are local, the taxonomy is deterministic categorisation against gold with no inference and no job, so $0 and the cap is untouched. I confirmed this by running an equivalent computation myself for q2 at $0. The ordering argument — reword first so the taxonomy cannot be read as confirming the wording it was run to test — is correct and is the right instinct.
dispositions_whose_reasoning_i_checked_a.12.2 — moot in part, descoped in part: Sound, and correctly ruled stratum by stratum rather than wholesale. Five of six strata are empty (three need an accepted set, one needs accepted cases, one needs the sealed shift split), and the frozen stratified sample cannot be constructed as specified from the sixth alone. Constructing a different sample after seeing the result is what 'frozen before reading examples' exists to prevent.
dispositions_whose_reasoning_i_checked_a.12.3 — executed as a binding constraint: Sound and correct. Section 12.3 is the authority O2 was raised under and it did bind.

q8_are_the_section_11_and_12_disposition.one_observation_about_the_document_as_a_: It is a good document and it does what O1 asked: every sub-item is ruled individually, every mootness states its reason, and no descope is on cost. Its own header records it as proposed and pending independent review, which is the right posture. R3 is the only correction.

nits.N1_generated_header_names_a_function_not: docs/writeup/claims-appendix.generated.md line 1 now reads 'GENERATED by: claims.render_surface(ledger, "report").' The previous header named `uv run conformalextract render-claims --surface report`, and that command does not exist — `uv run conformalextract --help` lists no `render-claims`, so replacing it was right. But a generated artifact's header should name something a reader can run. The runnable form is `uv run conformalextract verify-claims --surface report`, which is the CLI path to the same function at src/conformalextract/cli.py:1163, and on Windows it needs PYTHONUTF8=1 to survive the console encoding.
nits.N2_16x_over_the_baselines_is_only_true_o: '~16x reduction in ungrounded spans over the baselines' is 5,355 -> 340 against ZERO-SHOT, i.e. 15.75x. Against few-shot it is 2,875 -> 340, i.e. 8.5x. The plural 'baselines' is inherited from the old wording and is not introduced by this change, so it is a nit rather than a required item; but the change touched this clause and the ratio is now stated more precisely in every respect except which baseline it is measured against. 'over the zero-shot baseline' would close it.
nits.N3_wrong_is_binary_against_a_continuous_: 'is scored wrong anyway' predicates on the loss and is therefore safe, but a reader may attach it to the channel. The channel is not uniformly wrong: mean_loss_within_channel is 0.5793 (mean grounded-F1 about 0.42) and I measured 332 of its 2,847 documents at exactly zero loss. 'loses anyway' or 'is scored imperfectly anyway' would be exact at no cost in force.
nits.N4_limitation_5_points_at_a_limitation_t: New limitation 5 opens 'The reassurance in limitation 2 is operating-point-dependent'. Limitation 2 is 'Divergence is quality-neutral against gold and concentrates in low-confidence frames' — two findings, Follow-up 1 and Follow-up 2 of the probe.
